sanity_expectations: F_index is finite, real, and positive everywhere (v < p*(1-p) keeps the standardized variance v/(p(1-p)) < 1 across the whole region)
F_index increases monotonically with v at fixed p
F_index is O(0.1-0.7) over the sampled region; no blow-up because p stays in [0.2,0.8] away from 0/1
All four additive terms are positive over the region
excitation_report: sigma=0.005, k=5 (5*sigma=0.025), 512 Sobol samples over p in [0.2,0.8], v in [0.005,0.05]. Per-term multiples: base/inbreeding term 30.7x; drift term 32.4x; migration term 5.8x (rms 0.0288, above the 5x bar); NEW mutation term 50.3x (rms 0.251). New-term delta (E - parent) peak effect 0.281 = 56.3x, strongest at p~0.463, v~0.0052. No weak terms. Small deme (N=5) with m=0.2 gives N*m=1, the canonical regime where the 1/(4Nm+1) migration structure is non-negligible, so the migration term clears 5*sigma without unphysical values.
role_corrections: F_index: O->O (confirmed output; appears only on LHS, absent from RHS)
v: V->V (confirmed sampling axis; among-deme variance)
p: V->V (confirmed sampling axis; mean allele frequency)
migration_rate: V->P (overridden: phenomenon samples only v and p; m is a fixed model parameter, and it enters nonlinearly so it is not a sampling axis)
rationale: Static algebraic relation F_index = RHS with F_index only on the LHS -> explicit, evaluated pointwise (evaluate_explicit). analyze_expression found no derivatives, integral kernels, or applied functions, confirming a non-dynamical record. Independent axes are v and p (the quantities researchers vary per the phenomenon); all other free symbols are fixed physical parameters. migration_rate was relabeled from axis to parameter: the phenomenon only varies v and p, and m enters nonlinearly (numerator and denominator), so auto_balance's attempt to treat it as a linear coefficient drove it to an unphysical 8.84 and was rejected. Parameters were set to physical values and confirmed with excitation_check: deme_size=5 with migration_rate=0.2 (N*m=1) makes the migration term clear 5*sigma, and every term including the new recurrent-mutation term is visible above sigma=0.005.

scenario_text: In a subdivided population, alleles are distributed unevenly among local demes, reducing overall heterozygosity relative to a panmictic expectation. A structure index quantifies the reduction in heterozygosity caused by variance in allele frequency among demes. Researchers sample populations with differing among-deme frequency variance and mean allele frequency to record the structure index. Mating within each deme is random.
